articleTitle: Enhancing Yoga Pose Recognition Using Large Language Models with Real-World Dataset Integration for Personalized Fitness Assistance
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: Correct detection of yoga poses has become a central aspect of personalized fitness to promote increased performance and enjoyment. This is further extended by the implementation of large language models, possibly complemented by real-world dataset-based information, to significantly contribute to a more accurate, flexible approach toward yoga detection. Using publicly available datasets such as the Yoga-82 dataset, the research leverages a rich amount of real-world variations in pose execution, lighting conditions, and background environments for the purpose of training robust recognition models. Incorporation of LLM facilitates nuanced interpretation and contextual understanding of pose data, allowing the system to offer tailored feedback and guidance to practitioners. In addition, the approach taken in this work emphasizes scalability and accessibility, ensuring that personalized fitness assistance can be seamlessly integrated with mobile and wearable technologies. The results of the experiments show significant improvements in the accuracy of recognition and user satisfaction, further underlining the promising use of LLM combined with real-world data in next-generation fitness applications. It paves the way for more intelligent and responsive fitness p latforms that cater to individual needs by fostering sustained engagement and healthier living.

articleTitle: Waste Definition and Identification in Software Engineering: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: Defining and identifying waste associated with software is a hot topic in the information technology industry. Therefore, on this paper we went through literature searching for definitions of software waste in general, then with more focus on waste in the context of software architecture. Then, we tried to identify the influential factors for the presence of waste along with its relationships with architectural technical debt and architectural bad smell. The majority of the definitions of waste focused on value delivery aspects of waste, as if the software component is not adding value to the end-users is considered as waste. Adding to that there were links between the presence of waste in the context of software architecture and architectural technical debt and architectural bad smell.

articleTitle: Deep Learning-Driven Cybersecurity Threat Detection and Mitigation in Saudi Arabia Healthcare System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: Cybersecurity threats in the healthcare industry, particularly in Saudi Arabia, pose significant challenges. As institutions adopt digital technologies under Saudi Arabia's Vision 2030, vulnerabilities to ransomware, phishing, and data breaches escalate. This paper investigates the role of Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (Bi-LSTM) and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) models in enhancing threat detection and mitigation strategies tailored to Saudi Arabia's unique healthcare requirements. The proposed model achieves 94 % accuracy, with high precision, recall, and F1-score, confirming its reliability in identifying cyber threats. Additionally, we introduce a hybrid deep learning architecture that integrates real-time threat monitoring and adaptive mitigation strategies. Experimental results demonstrate its effectiveness in safeguarding sensitive health care data and ensuring service continuity. These findings underscore the potential of deep learning in strengthening cybersecurity defenses in critical sectors.

articleTitle: Enhanced Intrusion Detection System for IoMT Devices Using Improved Human Evolutionary Optimization Algorithm and Tabular Transformers
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: The Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) has revolutionized healthcare by enabling real-time monitoring, intelligent diagnostics, and remote patient care. However, the widespread adoption of IoMT devices has introduced significant cybersecurity challenges. An Intrusion Detection System (IDS) is an essential tool designed to overcome these cybersecurity threats. This research presents a novel Intrusion Detection System (IDS) framework namely IHEOA-Tab that combines Improved Human Evolutionary Optimization Algorithm (IHEOA) for feature selection and Tabular Transformers for classification. First, healthcare intrusion detection system dataset namely CIC-IoMT2024 has been selected. Second, an improvement to the existing Human Evolutionary algorithm has been proposed. Besides, this IHEOA is used for selecting the crucial features from the dataset. Third, Tabular Transformers with self-attention mechanisms is employed for building the model and test it. The proposed model is evaluated using various performance measures such as accuracy, precision, recall and F1-score and confusion matrix in both binary and multiclass classification. The model achieved near-perfect classification performance, with minimal misclassifications.

articleTitle: Improving Alpha-Beta Pruning Efficiency in Chess Engines
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: Alpha-Beta Pruning is a critical optimization technique in chess engines, helping them make fast, accurate decisions by reducing unnecessary calculations. This paper focuses on enhancing its efficiency to improve search depth and speed with-out compromising accuracy. This investigation examines current challenges in traditional implementations, such as inefficiencies in move ordering and redundant computations, especially in complex game scenarios. The proposed innovative strategies include dynamic move ordering powered by machine learning and improved transposition table management. These techniques streamline the pruning process, ensuring the most promising moves are evaluated first and avoiding repetitive calculations. Adaptive depth control is explored to make the algorithm more responsive to the game's context. Extensive testing on various chess positions demonstrated clear improvements in pruning efficiency. The enhanced algorithm can analyze deeper game trees with reduced computational costs, making chess engines faster and smarter. These advancements not only benefit chess engines but also have broader implications for Artificial Intelligence (AI) systems requiring efficient decision-making in dynamic environments. Improved Alpha-Beta Pruning methods make chess engines smarter and faster, allowing them to analyze deeper strategies while using less computing power.

articleTitle: An Optimal Cipher Algorithm for Wireless Sensor Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: Recent advances in wireless technologies have led to an unprecedented growth in the number and variety of devices connected to networks. These devices collect, process, and transmit massive volumes of data. A major concern for wireless sensor networks is the protection of the transmitted data. In recent years, various lightweight encryption algorithms have been proposed to ensure the security of data transmitted through IoT networks. Symmetric key ciphers, particularly block ciphers, play a crucial role in securing devices. While the RECTANGLE algorithm is effective in encryption, it lacks sufficient confusion and diffusion properties essential for robust security. To address these limitations, we enhanced the RECTANGLE algorithm by incorporating a 3D cipher and modifying the key scheduling algorithm. Security analysis and performance tests were conducted to evaluate the effectiveness of the proposed algorithm. The results showed that the enhanced algorithm outperforms its original version, achieving a 51%-bit error rate in sensitivity to both key changes and plaintext variations, demonstrating improved cryptographic strength.

articleTitle: Generating Questions Bank for Adaptive Assessment Using Machine Learning Techniques: Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: Adaptive assessments have redefined educational evaluation by offering personalized and dynamic testing tailored to individual learner abilities. This paper reviews key advancements in adaptive assessment systems, emphasizing the integration of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning (ML) to enhance question generation, difficulty prediction, and proficiency estimation. It explores traditional and adaptive frame-works, including Computerized Adaptive Testing (CAT) and psychometric theories like Item Response Theory (IRT). Through a comparative analysis of recent studies, the paper highlights innovative algorithms, challenges in scalability and fairness, and opportunities for future research. The findings underscore the transformative potential of adaptive assessments in creating equitable and efficient educational environments. This review not only synthesizes current advancements but also identifies critical gaps and proposes future research directions for more inclusive and scalable adaptive assessment systems.

articleTitle: Predicting Supply Chain Disruptions Using Neural Network Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: The supply chain represents the entire product life cycle, from raw materials to the final product's delivery to the customer. Delivery delays are a significant risk that can affect both business operations and customer satisfaction. Such delays can lead to financial losses and diminished customer trust in the service provided. This study aims to propose a model for predicting late deliveries in the event of supply chain disruptions. A multilayer perceptron (MLP) neural network has been used to predict late deliveries for both multi-class and binary classifications, with Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Logistic Regression serving as benchmarks. The models were compared based on accuracy, precision, recall, and F1 score in the provided dataset and the study concludes that the hyper-parameters of the MLP model, such as hidden layers and learning rate, significantly affect its accuracy. The key findings of this research indicates that the tuning hyper parameters and learning rate resulted in varying outcomes and found that MLP model outperforms for binary classification, while in multi-class classification, the MLP, Logistic Regression, and SVM models produced similar results. However, the MLP model achieved the highest accuracy for binary classification.

articleTitle: Machine Learning for Medical Conditions SMOTE-Based Data Balancing Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: This project will require a medical conditions dataset to build a predicting model that can classify the level of health risk and medical conditions based on various clinical and demographic features. With this, the major objective is always the identification of different levels of health risk based on other metrics like BMI and blood pressure or glucose. Other types of demographic factors considered are gender and smoking status. All the missing values in the columns of numerical variables were imputed by median values so as to prevent any skew in the results even though part of the data were not complete; categorical features that include gender and smoking status were changed into dummy variables. This helps in ensuring such features are in a machine-friendly format. Numerical features are standardized to bring the scale of the feature to a standard, procedure that typically improves the model's performance by not allowing features with larger ranges from dominating the model. Therefore, through an analysis of these features, this project should help identify risk factors that can contribute to poor health outcomes and subsequently come up with a framework that predicts This kind of predictive model crucial in healthcare, A set of Exploratory Data Analyses (EDA) were performed in order to understand the relations between the features and the overall nature of the data through series of experiments. Distributions of the features are visualized by histograms, for any categorical variables bar plots represent, and numerical features draw potential interdependencies via their correlation heatmaps. Similarly, for some features pair-plots are generated while in case of exploring any type of a linear or non-linear kind ofrelationship that would highly affect the prediction generated through the model. Finally, the random forest classifier model was fitted to predict specific health conditions based on the feature set extracted. The dataset was split for training and testing purposes (70% 30%). Model performance for precision, recall, and F1-score were noted. Such an analysis presents the strength of the predictive model concerning accuracy and its feasibility in clinical screening applications. In summary, the project will provide a systematic approach toward predicting health risks and conditions through careful data preprocessing, exploratory analysis, and a robust classification model.

articleTitle: Explainable AI Model for Automatic Irrigation System using IOT
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: This paper presents an explainable artificial intelli-gence (XAI) model for automatic irrigation systems using Inter-net of Things (IoT) technology. The proposed system integrates soil moisture sensors, temperature sensors, and humidity sensors with a microcontroller to make data-driven irrigation decisions. A Random Forest classifier i s employed top redict irrigation requirements based on environmental parameters, with SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations) values providing transparency and interpretability of model decisions. The system demonstrates a 35 % reduction in water usage and a 20 % increase in crop yield compared to traditional irrigation methods. The integration of explainability enhances user trust and system adoption, making advanced agricultural technology accessible to farmers with varying technical expertise. Experimental results show that the Random Forest model outperforms XGBoost and SVM in accuracy (75%), precision (100% for non-irrigation decisions), and robustness for irrigation management.

articleTitle: Enhancing Healthcare Accessibility: A RAG- Based Medical Chatbot Using Transformer Models
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: Significant improvements in patient involvement and medical diagnosis have resulted from the use of AI in healthcare. This paper introduces a transformer-based medical chatbot that uses LangChain and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to provide accurate, context-aware healthcare support. The chatbot solves issues with healthcare accessibility, especially in underprivileged areas, and improves user happiness and diagnostic accuracy by utilizing large medical datasets. The aim of the work is to produce dependable and contextually relevant responses by refining refined LLaMa models using RAG approaches. It also looks at how AI-powered chatbots might help with data privacy, timely medical advice, and healthcare disparity reduction. The results highlight how AI-powered virtual health assistants might improve clinical judgment, lessen the workload for medical staff, and offer affordable patient care options.

articleTitle: Hybrid Approach: Combining Hill Climbing and Genetic Algorithms for Traveling Salesman Problem
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: The Traveling Salesman Problem (TSP) is a classic NP-hard optimization challenge, requiring an efficient approach to identify near-optimal solutions. This paper presents a hybrid algorithm combining Genetic Algorithm (GA) and Hill Climbing (HC) to improve solution accuracy and convergence speed. GA provides global search capabilities through selection, crossover, and mutation, while HC enhances local optimization by refining solutions iteratively. The hybrid approach leverages GA's exploration strength and HC's exploitative power, reducing premature convergence and improving search efficiency. Experimental results indicate that the hybrid GA-HC algorithm outperforms standalone GA and HC in terms of tour length reduction and computational efficiency. Benchmarked on TSP instances, the proposed method demonstrates a 15% improvement in solution quality compared to traditional approaches. Additionally, the hybrid method achieves faster convergence, requiring 30% fewer iterations than standalone GA. The results highlight the hybrid algorithm's potential for real-world applications such as logistics, network design, and supply chain management. This study contributes to the growing research on hybrid metaheuristics, showcasing the benefits of integrating global and local search strategies to solve complex combinatorial problems.

articleTitle: Optimizing Defect Detection in Photovoltaic Systems Using Machine Learning Based Approaches
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: For the renewable energy systems, it is imperative to ensure the efficiency and sustainability of the renewable energy system. Photovoltaic (PV) systems are a major contributor in the renewable energy systems. This paper addresses the role of machine learning in optimizing the defect detection in the PV modules using electroluminescence (EL) images. Firstly, the features are extracted using histogram of gradients (HOG) as it is a robust method for capturing the spatial and structural patterns from EL images. Then we investigate the effectiveness of feature selection methods using particle swarm optimization (PSO), genetic algorithm and Bayesian optimization to enhance the defect detection accuracy. The selected features are used to classify defective and non-defective PV cells using the machine learning algorithms namely support vector machines (SVM) and random forest classifiers. The performance of each optimization algorithm is assessed using performance metrics such as accuracy, precision, recall and F1-score. By optimizing feature selection and improving defect detection, this study contributes to enhance the operational efficiency of PV systems. The PSO method for optimized feature selection combined with SVM for defect detection outperformed the other two optimization algorithms giving an accuracy of 85% and precision of 91% on the public EL images dataset used in this work. This work aligns with the global efforts to promote sustainable energy by reducing the losses and improving the maintenance strategies and provides insights for integrating intelligent defect detection frameworks into renewable energy systems.

articleTitle: Meta-Learning-Driven QoS Estimation for Self-Optimizing 6G Networks in Stochastic α-η-µ Fading Channels with Multi-Layer Selection Combining and Cross-Layer Interference Adaptation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: The authors proposed to use a meta-learningbased approach for QoS optimization in future 6G networks that are self-optimizing sections, focusing on stochastic α − η − µ fading channels. The proposed model utilizes information learned in the past so that it can rapidly adapt to these changes as they arrive, providing much better area adaptation, energy efficiency and interference mitigation than traditional learning approaches. You push the best and QoS, network throughput, latency abased simulation results are provided under high mobility in addition to severe fading conditions. The metalearning model showed accelerated convergence, adaptive resource allocation and improved interference mitigation which naturally led to QoS improvement up to 80% as well energy efficiency increased up to 65−90%, network reliability were enhanced. This step helps build green and robust communication mechanisms in the next-generation networks.

articleTitle: Cryptanalysis of the Bluetooth Security Protocol Using Enhanced DNA Sticker Model
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: E0 is a robust stream cipher algorithm that is commonly used in Bluetooth security protocols. The algorithm works by using linear feedback shift registers to generate a stream of keys. These keys are then used to encrypt data. We can consider the method used to generate these keys to be based on propositional logic. The inputs for this logic are the outputs of the linear feedback shift registers, and the output is the binary sequence of the final key string. To construct a tube that collects the correct memory complexes, each step depends on a satisfying bit determined within the folds of the final key sequence, Zi. We have enhanced the sticker model to make it more effective in E0 cryptanalysis. This includes converting sequential search for all initial values of the shift registers into parallel search and changing the dependence of the decision on the logical variables of the regions individually. To launch an attack on E0 Algorithm, you would need to perform 237operations and know at most 200 key stream bits from the first frame of the output cipher text. Compared to earlier attacking algorithms, this is the best result achieved so far.

articleTitle: Forecasting Methane Emissions in Kuwait by 2030: A Time Series Approach Using ARIMA
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: Global methane emissions present a major challenge for climate change mitigation, with industrial and agricultural activities contributing significantly to greenhouse gas concentrations. This research applies the ARIMA (Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average) model to forecast Kuwait's annual methane emissions, projecting an annual growth rate of 3.70% between 2023 and 2030. By analyzing historical emissions data from 1850 to 2022, the research provides essential information for environmental policymaking. The model's validation via the autocorrelation function (ACF) and the partial autocorrelation function (PACF) highlights the strengths and limitations of the method. The forecasts emphasize the urgent necessity for targeted emission reduction policies with potential improvements, including the incorporation of explanatory variables, aggregate methods, and regional structural factors.

articleTitle: Transformational Leadership Style and Knowledge Management Role and Their Influence on Innovation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: Research objectives: This research explores transformational leaders and knowledge management and their role and influence on several pillars such as innovation, organizational performance, sustainable performance, and knowledge sharing and trust. Methodology: Systematic Literature Review is conducted by searching Scopus 23 studies were reviewed and included, focusing on knowledge management and transformational leadership style. Findings that transformational leadership and knowledge management are keys to drive innovation, sustainability, organizational performance and significantly knowledge sharing and trust. Originality/ Value Knowledge management and the role of transformational leadership are important topics for researchers, policy makers and practitioners.

articleTitle: A Secure and Privacy-Centric Blockchain Platform for Cloud-Based Healthcare Data Management
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: Privacy and security are major issues for healthcare data management in cloud environment. Blockchain technology guarantees data integrity, patient-centric control, and confidentiality, therefore providing a decentralized method to handle such problems. The presented paper suggests a blockchain-based system including decentralized storage, smart contracts, and advanced cryptography approaches. To effectively control healthcare data, the platform combines a consortium blockchain model, off-chain cloud storage, and userfriendly access for stakeholders. The reviews of performance have shown a 40% transaction cost decrease, a 50% throughput increase, and a 35% decrease in the level of latency. Based on the regulatory guidelines worldwide such as the HIPAA and GDPR, the present work emphasizes the way that the system could lead to revolutionizing the management of the health-care data.

articleTitle: Streamflow Prediction of Cañas River Watershed, Cavite, Philippines using Long Short-Term Memory
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: Cavite is a highly urbanized province situated near Metro Manila and has the highest population growth rate in the country. Water resource management and water-related risk mitigation is one of the major challenges the province faces. Cañas River Watershed is one of the major river systems in the province which covers major cities and municipalities. Effective streamflow monitoring in this watershed has not been achieved due to the inadequacy of monitoring stations around the province. This study aimed to develop an LSTM model to predict the streamflow in Cañas River Watershed at the Panaysanayan river gauge using the available weather parameters in two weather stations in the province, namely: Sangley Point Synoptic Station and Cavite State University (CvSU) Agrometeorological Station. Using the short-term data dated from 2014 to 2019 obtained from the stations and the river gage, the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model successfully predicted the streamflow. Based on the model performance evaluation the values of Nash-Sutcliffe Efficiency (NSE) for the training and test were 0.90-0.91 and 0.87-0.89, respectively which indicates a high predictive accuracy. On the other hand, the Percent Bias (PBIAS) results in training and testing ranges 0.60% -8.04% and 1.92% -8.32%, respectively, which indicates a low bias prediction. The model tends to underestimate values, especially high magnitude flows. The RMSE-to-Standard Deviation Ration (RSR) results in training and testing ranges from 0.30-0.31 and 0.34-0.35, respectively, which indicates a good predictive power. The model results also show a good performance in developing a flow duration curve in the river to determine its dependable flow. The R2-value between the observed and predicted flow at different probability of exceedance is 0.9938. The dependable flow of Cañas River Watershed at Panaysanayan river gauge was 60 liters per second based on the observed flows and 61.12 liters per second based on the predicted flows.

articleTitle: Adaptive Stream Processing Framework for Smart City IoT Networks Using Self-Powered Photodetector-based Data Collection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: This paper presents the Adaptive Resource Allo-cation for Stream Processing (ARASP) framework, a novel approach integrating self-powered photodetector-based sensors with intelligent stream processing for smart city IoT networks. The framework achieves 94.8 % reduction in processing latency (45±3ms) compared to traditional systems while improving resource utilization by 89.2% (94.2% efficiency) a nd energy sustainability by 96.8 % across 14 international deployments. Our photodetector network, operating in the 200-980nm spectrum, demonstrates 85 % energy harvesting efficiency through a dual-mode system combining photovoltaic and pyro-phototronic ef-fects. The adaptive resource allocator employs machine learning algorithms that reduce operational costs by 47 % while main-taining performance stability across diverse environmental con-ditions, from −30°C to +48°C. Comparative analysis with existing frameworks shows ARASP outperforms current solutions by 45% in latency reduction, 35 % in resource optimization, and 28 % in adaptation capabilities. Six-month stability testing confirms consistent performance across variable workloads, establishing ARASP as a viable solution for sustainable smart city infras-tructure with significant improvements i n both computational efficiency and environmental adaptability.

articleTitle: Multi-Task Learning Approach for Simultaneous Prediction of Multiple Comorbidities in Diabetic Patients
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: The proposed work gives a Multi-Task Learning (MTL) mechanism for the simultaneous predictions of multiple comorbidities in diabetic patients, aiming to improve early detection and personalized healthcare treatment strategies. By leveraging MTL, the proposed model will train to predict multiple comorbid conditions such as cardiovascular-related disease, kidney-affecting disease, and even neuropathy in a single unified methodology. The model uses shared representations across tasks while allowing for task-specific metrics, enhancing prediction accuracy by learning the interdependencies between comorbidities. A Supervised learning algorithm like a deep neural structured network (DNN) is used, where the input features include the patient's demographical type data, past medical history, laboratorybased results, and clinically given measurements. The model is trained using a vast dataset of diabetic patients, and the multitask learning schema is optimized through backpropagation. Performance Evaluation metrics like sugar levels, BP analysis, and heartbeat rate are utilized to assess the model's performance. The results showcase the effectiveness of the MTL mechanism in capturing the underlying relationships between comorbidities, outperforming single-task models in both prediction accuracy rate and computational efficacy. This framework can potentially assist healthcare providers in delivering a more comprehensive way of care for diabetic patients with multiple comorbidities.

articleTitle: Transforming Digital Images Into Cartoon Styles Visual Using Convolutional Neural Networks
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: The art of cartoonization in images has garnered significant attention, especially with the breakthroughs witnessed in entertainment, digital art, and social media.The traditional methods rely on the carted filters and edge detection techniques, which sometimes fail to retain the important features in the image.This paper proposes a deep learning-based technique using convolutional neural network (CNN) to apply this cartoon effect.Readjusted description of CNN addition works-detection, feature extraction from real-world images, edge enhancement, color quantization, and finally achieve quality outputs as outputs.A diverse dataset of real as well as cartoon images was used for training our model, while it was optimized by loss functions such as MSE and perceptual losses. The proposed approach is evaluated for structural similarity, perceptual quality, and computational efficiency. Indexed databases demonstrated that our approach is better than traditional approaches as it creates appealing cartoon-type outputs while significantly keeping content integrity intact. This work will contribute to an ever-growing time with great relevance to various AI-enabled artistic transformations which can be of great use in digital media, animated storytelling, and creative content generation.

articleTitle: Collaboration of AI with Project Management
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: In the area of driving technologies, synthetic intelligence (AI) is unexpectedly growing, and is opening manner for a future that's mostly led using the technology. Project control constitutes a crucial role in the modern and fast-changing environment. This paper focuses on the relationship between Artificial intelligence and Human Intelligence in performing control, with a view to identifying challenges and recommending appropriate solutions and approaches. The efficiency of AI and human collaboration for the enhancement of adaptive project management in dynamic environments. It works to combine the talents of human beings and the practicality of advanced computation to improve enterprise management. Dealing with the jobs at the same time in the changing environment is one of the large aspects that are involved in the control in undertaking and the same has been highlighted in the trouble statement. Project managers can turn out to be extra adaptable through the usage of both human creativity and synthetic intelligence ability in complicated situations, which regularly present challenging issues.

articleTitle: JAYA based Classifier System for Cybersecurity
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: Cybersecurity incidents, whether due to human actions or natural disasters, are becoming a significant threat to businesses, organizations, and governments. The frequency of cyber-attacks is increasing, and these attacks can spread quickly through platforms such as flash devices and hard disks. Protecting a network from such threats is the foremost priority, and an intrusion detection system (IDS) plays a key role. An IDS monitors networks and analyzes data to identify abnormal or malicious activity. This study proposes a new method for strengthening our defense against cybersecurity threats by integrating the Jaya algorithms with classification systems. We used optimization techniques to increase the efficiency of these models in countering cyberattacks by applying JAYA algorithms instead of known and regular genetic units, that is, genetic algorithms. We introduce a Jaya-based framework that optimizes the breeding classifier, namely, the feed classification system, to improve detection accuracy. The primary experimental results indicate that the proposed work's detection rate (DR) exceeds 90% with a false alarm rate of less than 5%. All experiments were conducted on the UNSW-NB15 dataset to demonstrate the detection efficiency.

articleTitle: A Comparative Analysis of Deep Neural Network Models for Deepfake Image Detection Generated using AI
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: Deepfake consists of two words - “deep” and “fake,” where deep refers to the deep neural network and fake indicates the manipulation of data. The gradual increase in usage of AI-generated images poses serious concerns and threats as these kinds of images challenge the authenticity of images and videos. This manipulation of pictures should be addressed to reduce their misuse in spreading misinformation, identity theft, and other malicious activities. This study mainly focuses on developing a model that can help detect the use of deepfake images. We used convolutional neural networks (CNNs) together with advanced architectures ResNet50 and XceptionNet to classify whether an image is real or fake. We trained our model on two different datasets and compared their accuracies. These datasets contained authentic as well as deepfake images which are used for the model's training and testing. Comparing the three models, it is found that the XceptionNet architecture performed classification with an accuracy of 84%. To enhance detection accuracy, preprocessing techniques are also applied to extract meaningful features and reduce noise in the data.

articleTitle: MindMedix: An AI-Powered Platform for Neurological Diagnosis and Personalized Treatment
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: Neurological diseases such as Stroke, Tumors, and Alzheimer's disease pose major challenges to healthcare systems worldwide. Rapid and accurate diagnosis is essential for timely treatment, but traditional diagnostic methods are often ineffective, leading to misdiagnosis and treatment delays. MindMedix, an AI-powered platform, aims to revolutionize the diagnosis and treatment of neurological diseases. By integrating patient medical history, symptoms, and MRI data, it provides highly accurate and personalized treatment recommendations. The platform leverages deep learning techniques and Explainable AI (XAI) models to enhance decision-making and ensure interpretability. MindMedix reduces diagnostic errors, minimizes wait times, and improves patient outcomes. The study presents a comparative analysis of existing AI-based diagnostic tools, demonstrating MindMedix's superior accuracy and efficiency.

articleTitle: HESTStream: A Hybrid Edge-Stream $C_{\text{opt}}$ and $PR_{\text{eff}}$ Processing Framework for Sustainable Smart Cities Using Adaptive Caching and Environmental Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: This paper presents HESTStream, a novel hybrid edge-stream processing framework that integrates environmental monitoring with real-time data analytics for sustainable smart cities. The framework addresses key challenges in stream pro-cessing by implementing an adaptive hash-based hybrid caching model (HCache) combined with distributed sensor networks. Our approach leverages triboelectric sensors and edge computing to enable real-time environmental monitoring while optimizing power consumption and data processing efficiency. Experimental results across 14 international deployment sites demonstrate that HESTStream achieves 47% improved processing latency, 38% reduced power consumption, and 42% enhanced cache hit ratio compared to existing methods. The framework provides a scalable solution for smart city applications requiring real-time environmental data processing while maintaining sustainability goals.

articleTitle: Generating Questions Bank for Adaptive Assessment Using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: This research investigates the core components and machine learning techniques essential for adaptive assessment processes. It aims to propose a comprehensive system design, evaluate the effectiveness of various machine learning approaches, and develop methodologies to utilize traditional assessment data for predicting question difficulty and learner proficiency levels. By leveraging response data of learners, the study seeks to create a dynamic question bank enriched with metadata, facilitating personalized adaptive assessments. The findings aim to provide a robust framework for implementing adaptive assessments, thereby enhancing their adaptability and accuracy in evaluating learner performance.

articleTitle: Proactive Detection of Zero-Day Vulnerabilities in Industrial Control Systems Through Baseline Configuration Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: Industrial Control Systems (ICS) are vital to critical infrastructure, making their cybersecurity essential. This paper addresses the challenge of detecting zero-day vulnerabilities in ICS environments, where timely patching is critical to prevent disruption. “Baseline Configuration Checker,” a software tool designed by the authors to proactively identify deviations in Windows service configurations against vendor-defined baselines. Through real-time comparison and analysis of service attributes, the engine enables the detection of potential vulnerabilities introduced by misconfigurations or unauthorized modifications. Evaluation in a controlled ICS lab environment demonstrates the engine's high accuracy in detecting deviations, facilitating proactive vulnerability management and enhancing ICS security.

articleTitle: A System to Detect Unconscious Bias Using Virtual Patients - System Architecture
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: The implementation of unconscious bias training within the workplace promotes diversity, safety, and respect by aiding individuals in recognizing, managing, and mitigating their biases. Simulation-based training, which effectively mirrors real-world situations, has gained popularity among healthcare professionals. This training approach enables patients to make errors, engage in learning, reflect on their experiences, receive constructive feedback, and enhance their clinical competencies while prioritizing patient safety. However, immersive technology simulations are not without their challenges, including latency issues and difficulties with spatial awareness. This study provides an overview of the system domain and includes a traceability diagram outlining the logical and physical architecture. This paper is the fourth installment in a series dedicated to the development of a virtual patient system designed to evoke unconscious bias in medical students.

articleTitle: Evaluation of Secure Email Awareness: A Case Study
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: This study explores the level of awareness regarding secure email practices among university students in Bahrain and the UK, specifically focusing on their use of institutional email systems. Email is a primary communication tool in academia, yet students often demonstrate limited awareness of essential security measures, such as encryption and signing. The research investigates the frequency with which students use email for both academic and personal purposes, providing context for the importance of secure email practices. Additionally, the study examines students’ awareness of common email-related threats, including phishing, hacking, and data breaches. It also assesses whether students engage in proactive security measures, such as scanning email attachments for malware, verifying senders through email signing, and using encryption to protect sensitive information. By comparing students from Bahrain and the UK, the study aims to identify any cultural, educational, or institutional factors influencing email security practices. The findings are expected to inform the development of targeted educational initiatives to enhance email security awareness, thereby equipping students to protect their email communications better, reduce exposure to cyber threats, and promote safer digital environments across both regions.

articleTitle: Integration of a Hybrid Model with XAI for Stock Price Forecasting: A Dashboard-Driven Approach
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: This paper on Integration of a Hybrid Model with XAI for Stock price Forecasting focuses on improving the accuracy and transparency of stock price predictions through a combined model of Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) and MultiProphet, with an emphasis on explainable artificial intelligence (XAI). LSTM which is a deep learning model, is good at identifying patterns in time-series data. while MultiProphet which is an enhanced version of Facebook's Prophet model, effectively handles seasonal variations and anomalies in financial data. By integrating both models, the hybrid approach delivers more reliable stock forecasting. In addition, this project integrates XAI techniques like SHAP and LIME to offer greater insight into how the model generates predictions, which is crucial for informed financial decision-making. Dynamic dashboard provides an intuitive interface for users to track stock price trends, view forecasts, and access explanations of the model's predictions in real-time. This combination of improved prediction accuracy and model transparency enables better decision-making by stakeholders, who can base their actions on clear and interpretable information. Overall, the project represents a significant advancement in making advanced AI models more accessible and actionable in practical, user-oriented financial applications.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning Approach to Predict Autism Spectrum Disorder
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder, often shortened to ASD, is a developmental disability caused by differences in the brain. Individuals with ASD display deficits in social communication and interaction as well as repetitive behaviors or interests among a list of other symptoms [1]. If left untreated, individuals with autism may observe no progression or a worsening of their symptoms as untreated ASD can increase the risk of the development of depression and anxiety. The best outcomes are expected when the individual is diagnosed as early as possible allowing for early intervention and the provision of therapy and treatments. ASD can be detected in individuals as young as toddlers. Much research has been conducted into the application of machine learning in order to predict ASD in many different age groups, with the category of toddlers having the least dedicated research. This paper aims to explore the application of different machine learning techniques in order to predict ASD in toddlers. Two different toddler datasets were used to train and test the models. Many different traditional machine learning models, ensemble models, and deep learning models were considered in the scope of this research and compared on the basis of performance. K-fold cross validation was applied, and the models were tested. The most positive results in terms of the highest accuracy recorded were seen in ensemble learning which near consistent positive results being seen for all the different experimented techniques. Further favorable results were seen in particular with random forest (100%), decision trees (100%), C4.5 (100%) and logistic regression (100%). In terms of deep learning the most positive results were seen in multilayer perceptron (100%), recurrent neural networks (98.6%), and multilayer kernel machines (100%).

articleTitle: OCT-CAD: An Automated Deep Learning Diagnostic Tool for Eye Diseases from Imbalanced OCT Scans
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: This work addresses the challenge of class imbalance in Optical Coherence Tomography (OCT). We propose OCT-CAD framework, a two-stream Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) for eye diseases classification. The proposed framework consists of two complimentary CNNs. One CNN is focused on classifying tail classes, and the other is focused on head classes. In the proposed framework, we utilize Key Point Sensitive Loss (LKPs) and Cross-Entropy Loss (LCE) to train the proposed framework. Then, the features extracted from the two CNNs are processed using PCA, DCT, and feature selection techniques to enhance the representation. The experimental results show that a stacking classifier that combined random forest and gradient boost achieves 100% accuracy on the OCTID dataset, demon-strating the effectiveness of the proposed OCT-CAD framework in addressing class imbalance, improving diagnostic performance and surpassing existing state-of-the-art techniques.

articleTitle: Harnessing Computational Intelligence: In-Depth Applications in Biology and Medicine
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: Computational Intelligence (CI) has significantly impacted biology and medicine by enhancing diagnostics, treatment planning, and biological research. CI techniques like artificial neural networks, fuzzy logic, and evolutionary algorithms have revolutionized diagnostics, treatment planning, and biological research by processing high-dimensional, nonlinear, and uncertain data. This study highlights the role of CI in advancing healthcare through innovations such as explainable AI, adaptive systems, and multimodal data fusion. While CI improves accuracy and personalization, challenges remain in data quality, interpretability, and computational demands. Integrative approaches, combining various CI techniques, are key in areas like drug discovery, personalized medicine, and disease modeling. Future research should focus on interdisciplinary collaboration, standardization, and ethical governance to ensure sustainable progress.

articleTitle: Early Stage Detection of Colorectal Cancer using Segmentation of Polyps
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: Colorectal Cancer(CRC) is a major health problem around the world, accounting for a high number of cancer related deaths. It is important to detect the polyp at the initial stage and remove it to prevent them from becoming cancerous. Colonoscopy is the standard examination for CRC, but pathologists face difficulties in detecting the polyps in the colonoscopy image due to the small size and the color contrast between the polyp and its background. Expert pathologists are very less in numbers compared with the cancer patients.therefore, an automated system is required to assist pathologists in the detection of polyps in early stage. Deep learning models help the pathologists to detect polyps at an early stage automatically that may be missed otherwise due to their small size, low contrast, and presence of extremely small polyps in a single image. We propose light weight model Transformer ResU- Net3plus (TransResU-Net3+) for automated segmentation of polyps in early stage of cancer. Proposed method consists of residual blocks using ResNet-50 as the backbone and also uses transformer self-attention and dilated convolutions. We have applied the proposed method on a publicly available dataset kvasir-seg and achieved an Intersection Over Union (IOU) of 0.892 and outperforms over existing state of the art methods on kvasir-seg dataset.

articleTitle: PSL-CFRT: A Benchmark Multi-View Dataset for Continuous Pakistani Sign Language Fingerspelling Recognition and Translation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: Fingerspelling, an essential component of sign language, utilizes distinct hand configurations for each letter of a written language to convey proper names, technical terms, addresses, numerical values, and other uncommon words. This intricate form of communication is challenging for the general community, creating a communication barrier between the deaf and hard-of-hearing (DHH) community and those unfamiliar with it. To bridge this gap, this paper introduces a novel multi-view dataset specifically designed for continuous fingerspelling recognition and translation in Pakistani Sign Language (PSL). This dataset is unique in its inclusion of diverse fingerspelling variations, enhancing its applicability to real-world scenarios. In addition to introducing the dataset, an object-detection-based method is proposed for PSL continuous fingerspelling recognition (PSL-CFR), marking a significant advancement in continuous PSL finger-spelling recognition technology, achieving a baseline accuracy of 63.16%.

articleTitle: Impact of Social Engineering on Social Media Users
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: This position paper examines the impact of social engineering attacks on social media users, focusing on how demographic factors, platform-specific risks, and user behavior influence susceptibility. The paper identifies key vulnerabilities in user behavior, such as oversharing personal information, which cybercriminals exploit to carry out manipulative attacks. It also explores the risks specific to various social media platforms and how these environments can be leveraged for malicious purposes. Furthermore, the paper proposes actionable recommendations for addressing these vulnerabilities, including awareness campaigns and design changes that can better protect users. The research contribution lies in offering a comprehensive understanding of how demographic factors and platform-specific risks intersect with user behavior, providing a foundation for more targeted interventions to reduce the impact of social engineering on social media users.

articleTitle: Markov Decision Processes in Autonomous Robot Navigation
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: This paper presents a comprehensive investigation of Markov Decision Processes (MDPs) in autonomous robot navigation, focusing on their application in dynamic and uncertain environments. MDPs provide a mathematical framework for modeling decision-making processes where outcomes are partially random and partially controlled by an autonomous agent. The research examines how MDPs enable robots to optimize their navigation strategies by balancing immediate rewards with long-term benefits, particularly in complex environments requiring real-time decision-making. The study implements a Reward-based Action Motion Deep Planning (RAMDP) system, integrating reinforcement learning techniques, specifically Q-learning, with traditional MDP frameworks. This integration enables robots to adapt their navigation strategies through experience and environmental feedback. The system's performance is evaluated across various environmental conditions, from simple to dynamic scenarios, measuring metrics including goal achievement rates, path optimization, and obstacle avoidance success. Results demonstrate significant improvements in navigation efficiency, with goal achievement rates maintaining above 80% even in dynamic environments. The system shows particular strength in real-time adaptability, effectively handling sudden obstacles and path blockages while maintaining energy efficiency. The implementation successfully balances computational efficiency with decision quality, making it suitable for real-world applications. This research contributes to the field of autonomous robotics by providing a robust framework for decision-making under uncertainty, offering practical solutions for challenges in robot navigation, and demonstrating the effectiveness of combining MDPs with modern machine learning techniques for improved autonomous navigation performance.

articleTitle: IPL Data Analysis by Web Scraping and Using PowerBI
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: Cricket fans throughout the world avidly follow the Indian Premier League (IPL), a competition of great fame. The IPL data is examined in this using Exploratory Data Analysis (EDA) approaches to find hidden trends, patterns, and insights. Key findings are summarized in EDA, a critical stage of data processing that is frequently complemented with visual aids. Through EDA, the goal is to investigate several factors, including team performance, player data, match results, and venue effects. Data transformation, cleaning, and visualization will all be part of producing insightful findings. Win percentages, player averages, and run distributions are examples of key performance indicators (KPIs) that will be looked at. The analysis's findings will give teams, athletes, and supporters important new information.

articleTitle: Exploring $\text{ZnA}1_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4}$ Nanoparticles for Wireless Applications: Insights from Sol-Gel Synthesis
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: The increasing demand for miniaturized and lightweight wireless microstrip patch antennas has driven extensive research into suitable dielectric materials. Zinc aluminate <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$(\text{ZnA}1_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4})$</tex> nanoparticles exhibit low dielectric loss and high permittivity, making them promising candidates for microwave applications. In this study, <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{ZnA}1_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4}$</tex> nanoparticles were synthesized using the sol-gel technique, and their chemical composition, morphology, structural, and dielectric properties were systematically investigated. X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis confirmed the formation of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{ZnA}1_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4}$</tex> with a crystallite size of 19.5 nm, corresponding to the <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{ZnO}$</tex> wurtzite phase. Dielectric permittivity measurements at <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$30^\circ\mathrm{C}, 40^\circ\mathrm{C}$</tex>, and <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$50^\circ\mathrm{C}$</tex> yielded values of 8.82, 8.80, and 8.78, respectively, while dielectric loss values were recorded as 0.06, 0.04, and 0.05. The results indicate that the dielectric loss decreases with increasing frequency, highlighting the suitability of <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\text{ZnA}1_{2}\mathrm{O}_{4}$</tex> nanoparticles for high-frequency microwave applications.

articleTitle: ESPEAR: Enhanced Stream Processing for Environmental Analytics and Renewable Energy Integration Using Smart Dielectric Sensors
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: This paper presents ESPEAR (Enhanced Stream Processing for Environmental Analytics and Renewable Energy), an innovative methodology integrating smart dielectric sensors with stream processing for environmental monitoring and renewable energy optimization. Building upon recent advances in green chemical reactions using inert solid dielectrics, we develop a comprehensive system that combines real-time environmental data processing with 5G millimeter-wave technology. The system implements the STAR cache-based warehouse architecture for efficient spatial data management while incorporating sustainable energy practices. Our experimental results across fourteen countries demonstrate significant improvements in processing efficiency (45%), energy consumption reduction (38%), and monitoring accuracy (92%) compared to existing methods. The implementation shows particular promise in smart city applications, achieving a 40% reduction in response latency while maintaining 99.9% system reliability.

articleTitle: Trusting Predictions of Acoustic Classification
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: Trusting the predictions of acoustic classifiers is crucial in today's military. Having confidence in the predictions of machine learning models used by military systems for surveillance, reconnaissance, or on the battlefield is essential for human adoption. If the system is unreliable, soldiers who could potentially benefit from its assistance may experience adverse effects. In light of this, we present an algorithm that calculates neural network classifier confidence scores, enabling us to assess the trustworthiness of classifiers. In this inquiry, we utilize the Latent Space-Statistical (LS-Stat) confidence score technique to compute the confidence score of an acoustic signal classifier. The LS-Stat approach utilizes the latent features extracted from the penultimate layer of the trained classifier model to compute the confidence score. The classifier model employs the Acoustic-Seismic Classification Identification Data Set (ACIDS) for training and validation. Using the trained classifier, the confidence scores of the classifier predictions are compared using LS-Stat, Monte Carlo dropout, and prediction probability values or SoftMax algorithms. Our findings indicate that the LS-Stat method outperforms the other methods in terms of accuracy, prediction, and confidence score.

articleTitle: Frame-Based Knowledge Representation for Intelligent Tutoring Systems
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: Frame-based knowledge representation has come as a robust paradigm for representing and organizing knowledge in Intelligent Tutoring Systems (ITS). Frames as mental constructs facilitate the representation of entities of the world, their char-acteristics, and associations and, thus, are particularly amenable to domain knowledge modeling, student profiles, and teaching tactics modeling in ITS. Developments in frame-based systems have more recently targeted the promotion of adaptability, per-sonalization, and scalability in tutoring systems. Researchers have incorporated frames into machine learning methods, including deep learning and reinforcement learning, to allow for dynamic knowledge updates and real-time adjustment according to stu-dent needs. In addition the integration of frame-based represen-tations with otologies and semantic web technologies enhanced interoperability and reasoning, enabling more precise diagnosis of student misconceptions and adaptive feedback generation. This work has also been investigated in collaborative learning contexts, where frames are used to represent group interactions and collective knowledge construction. In addition, the use of natural language processing (NLP) and frame-based representations has made it possible for ITS to improve comprehension and answer students' questions in natural language more effectively resulting in an enhanced user experience. Challenges persist nonetheless, including addressing the complexity of large-scale frame-based systems as well as making knowledge acquisition and maintenance efficient. This paper summaries the latest work on frame-based knowledge representation in ITS, major innovation, uses, and prospects. Through dealing with these problems, frame-based ITS can advance, providing even better and adaptive learning experiences to learners.

articleTitle: Automatic Microstructure Image Analysis for Predicting Metals Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: This paper presents a deep learning-based approach for automated microstructure classification in metallic materials. The model leverages convolutional neural networks (CNNs) with transfer learning to enhance accuracy and scalability, achieving a classification accuracy of 95%. Data augmentation was applied to address dataset constraints. This research provides a significant advancement in industrial applications such as aerospace and manufacturing, streamlining metallurgical analysis while improving reliability and decision-making.

articleTitle: Leveraging Mobile Applications for Social Entrepreneurship: Driving Innovation and Impact in a Digital Era
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: This review explores the intersection of mobile applications and social entrepreneurship, emphasizing their transformative potential in addressing social, economic, and environmental challenges. By integrating mobile technology, social entrepreneurs can significantly enhance operational efficiency, expand their reach, and develop innovative solutions tailored to the needs of underserved populations. Key areas of impact include healthcare, education, agriculture, and financial inclusion, where mobile applications have demonstrated substantial promise. However, the successful implementation of these technologies requires overcoming challenges related to financial constraints, technological adaptation, sustainability, and ethical considerations such as data privacy and security. The review underscores the importance of a supportive ecosystem, including favorable government policies, regulatory frameworks, and robust digital infrastructure, to maximize the potential of mobile applications in social entrepreneurship. Future directions should focus on fostering innovation and growth through continuous technological advancement, tailored functionality, and effective management of user expectations. By harnessing the capabilities of mobile technology, social entrepreneurs can drive meaningful and lasting societal change, contributing to a more equitable and sustainable future.

articleTitle: Enhancing the Detection of Automated DDoS Attacks Using Advanced Machine Learning Methods
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: Detecting Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) attacks remains a pivotal area of research, with machine learning (ML) methods playing a central role in identifying these attacks through flow-based characteristics. This study explored advanced ML models, ranging from traditional algorithms such as Logistic Regression, Decision Trees, Random Forest, and Gaussian Naive Bayes to state-of-the-art deep learning architectures, for anomaly-based DDoS detection systems (DDoSDS). Leveraging the CICIDS2017 dataset, we demonstrated the effectiveness of our approach in capturing complex attack patterns. We primarily focused on employing feature selection strategies, including Univariate Feature Selection (UFS) and Recursive Feature Elimination (RFE), to reduce dimensionality from 70 to 10 with minimal effect on model performance. These techniques not only enhanced detection accuracy to an impressive 99.99% but also significantly reduced false positives and false negatives, achieving a remarkable 0.0% in both metrics. This advancement offers a robust and reliable shield against evolving security threats, highlighting the transformative potential of ML in safeguarding network systems from DDoS attacks.

Index Terms: Distributed Denial Of Service Attack Detection

articleTitle: Empowering a Nutritional Lifestyle through Soaked and Streamed Nuts Water Reuse using Novel RNN and NLP
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: This study evaluates the effectiveness of a Novel Recurrent Neural Network (RNN) against Natural Language Processing (NLP) methods for nutrient extraction from soaked and steamed nut water. Research Instruments and Methodologies: Ten nutrients were retrieved utilizing advanced RNN and NLP approaches. The iteration value was estimated using G-power analysis with a power of 0.8 and a 95% confidence range. The findings indicated that the Novel RNN method attained an accuracy of 84.10%, surpassing the NLP approach's 71.48%. A statistical analysis indicated that the two approaches exhibited a substantial difference, evidenced by a two-tailed p-value of 0.000 (p < 0.05). The results indicate that the Novel RNN surpasses NLP methods in nutrient extraction accuracy, rendering it a more dependable option for this work.

articleTitle: Exercise Recognition and Analysis for Improved Fitness Tracking Using Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: The growing popularity of fitness tracking and wearable technologies has paved the way for more sophisticated methods of monitoring physical activities. This paper presents an exercise recognition framework designed to enhance fitness tracking by accurately identifying and classifying various physical exercises. The proposed framework uses wearable sensors, specif-ically smartphones equipped with accelerometers and gyroscopes, to collect motion data during different exercises. These exercises, including walking, walking up, walking down, running, and arm rotation, were selected to represent a variety of movement types to ensure robust classification. Several machine learning algorithms are explored, including random forest, and decision tree for the classification task. The Random Forest model outperformed other classifiers.

articleTitle: Predicting Co-Morbid Chronic Diseases: Hypertension and Diabetes Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: This research proposes a deep learning-oriented method for forecasting the co-morbidity of hypertension and diabetes utilizing Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs). The main contribution of this research is the creation of a hybrid deep learning framework that proficiently merges CNNs for feature extraction and RNNs for sequence modeling, facilitating precise disease prediction from electronic health records (EHR). The model is trained using a vast dataset that includes demographic, clinical, and lifestyle factors to improve predictive accuracy. Our experimental findings indicate that the proposed model attains 92.5% accuracy, 90.1% precision, and 88.7% recall, surpassing traditional machine learning techniques. Additionally, we incorporate SHAP (Shapley Additive Explanations) values to enhance model interpretability, enabling healthcare professionals to pinpoint essential risk factors that affect predictions. The results underscore the promise of deep learning in fostering early disease detection, streamlining patient care, and lowering healthcare expenses. This research establishes a base for prospective AI-driven predictive analytics in healthcare, with potential for real-world application and further advancement through federated learning and real-time clinical data integration.

articleTitle: Recurrent Neural for Time Series Prediction in Finance
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: Overcoming risk is crucial when predicting financial time series, such as stock prices, due to market volatility influenced by factors like economic reports, political events, and investor sentiment. Linear models like ARIMA handle linear dependencies well but fail to capture nonlinear relationships, which are key in financial forecasting. While Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) models excel at capturing temporal dependencies, they struggle with identifying significant market events, potentially contaminating predictions. This paper introduces an Attention RNN with Sentiment Integration, which combines Recurrent Neural Networks (RNN) with an attention mechanism for sentiment analysis of financial news and social media. The model considers relevant time steps and market sentiment, improving context-awareness. Results demonstrate that this hybrid approach outperforms traditional methods by providing a more accurate and flexible forecasting model, addressing the complexities of financial markets. Additionally, sentiment data helps the model capture both stock-specific and overall market sentiment, particularly during periods of heightened uncertainty or volatility, offering a more comprehensive approach to stock price prediction. Keywords: Risk, Financial Time Series, ARIMA, LSTM, Attention RNN, Sentiment Analysis, Market Sentiment, Stock Prices, Forecasting, Volatility.

articleTitle: Shake-to-Alert: An Automated Mobile Safety Application for Women with Emergency Notification via Motion Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: This project introduces a mobile application aimed at enhancing women's safety through a motion-triggered alert system. Utilizing the phone's accelerometer, the app detects intentional shakes and triggers an emergency alert. Upon activation, the app automatically sends a message to a pre-registered guardian contact, including the user's real-time GPS location. The GPS module ensures precise location tracking, while the GSM module sends the alert via SMS or notifications. The shake detection algorithm uses thresholds for motion intensity and duration to differentiate between accidental and intentional shakes. This system provides a quick, discreet, and reliable safety mechanism, empowering users with an easy-to-use tool for immediate help in emergencies. The integration of location tracking, real-time alerts, and motion detection creates a robust solution for women's personal security. The GPS module pinpoints the user's location, and the GSM module transmits the alert, even without internet access. The system runs in the background to allow discrete operation, ensuring that guardians receive continuous location updates if needed. This system offers an efficient, real-time solution for personal safety.

articleTitle: Enhancing Robustness of Fruit and Vegetable Image Classification Against Adversarial Attacks Through Defensive Strategies
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: Typically, machine learning models allow number of applications including recognition and classification. The adversarial machine learning attack fools the machine learning and deep learning models by initiating a noise attack over the models. The adversarial attack targets the machine learning models to harm the models in a way that the models start classifying the images incorrectly. This leads to increasing the error rate and decreasing the accuracy rate of the machine learning models. The attack is not visible to the human eye to detect. Only the machine learning models can detect the changes. Before and after the attack, all images look identical for the human eye. In this study, we introduce a deep learning model that classifies fruit and vegetable images. Then, we conduct an experiment on the deep learning model. The experiment has two folds, in the first fold we apply three different adversarial attack methods on the model which are the Fast Gradient Sign Method (FGSM), Iterative Fast Gradient Sign Method (I-FGSM) and Momentum Iterative Fast Gradient Sign Method (MI-FGSM). We measure the model's performance in term of accuracy scores before and after applying each attack. The model's performance degrades, and the accuracy scores drops down because of the adversarial attack methods. The scientific experiment we conduct shows the decrease in the accuracy scores over different values of epsilon. The second fold of the study is implementing three different defense strategies into the model which are the distilled neural network, adversarial training, and binary thresholding. We measure the model's performance after applying the defense strategies individually. The model becomes more robust against the adversarial attack, and the accuracy scores of the model increases because of the defense lines incorporated into the model. The experimental results show that only the distilled neural network and the adversarial training strategies successfully protected the model against the adversarial attack.

articleTitle: Systematic Literature Review of Adopting AI Robots in the UAE Judicial System
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: This position paper explores the potential integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) robots into the judicial system of the United Arab Emirates (UAE). It evaluates the opportunities and challenges associated with employing AI in legal services, particularly in areas such as reliability, security, confidentiality, and ethical considerations. The paper emphasizes the lack of existing regulations addressing the accountability of AI robots compared to human legal professionals. It proposes the need for a legal framework to support this transition. By conducting a systematic literature review, the study draws comparisons between global implementations of AI in judicial systems and identifies key gaps and limitations. The findings aim to guide policymakers and stakeholders in aligning AI advancements with the UAE's legal and ethical standards. Although the research is ongoing, this paper outlines critical hypotheses and raises questions about the trustworthiness of AI robots in providing unbiased legal advice and protecting sensitive client data. The study contributes to the vision of a zerobureaucracy government and offers preliminary recommendations for integrating AI robots into the UAE's judicial framework.

articleTitle: The Socioeconomic and Technological Implications of 5G Deployment in Urban and Rural Communities of South Africa
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: The global challenge of accessing mobile broadband networks persists, with various stakeholders undertaking several initiatives to address this issue. Among these, the rollout and deployment of 5G technology is considered a significant effort to bridge the digital divide. 5G is recommended due to its capacity to provide short- and longdistance coverage, facilitating network access in urban and rural areas. However, 5G adoption has been more prevalent in urban areas than in rural communities. This disparity is primarily attributed to infrastructure availability, return on investment, radio frequency spectrum limitations, and policy challenges. This paper examines the adoption of 5G in both urban and rural contexts within South Africa (SA) while identifying critical issues and areas where policy and regulatory interventions may be necessary. To achieve this, a qualitative desktop research approach through secondary research was employed, analyzing publicly available information, including journal articles, policy documents related to the 5G rollout in urban and rural areas, and other academic sources. Primary data collection through interviews was also conducted to engage key stakeholders to understand their viewpoints and perceptions about the 5G rollout. The key findings from the study demonstrate that the 5G network benefits urban areas, whilst rural communities remain underserved due to weak policy and lack of infrastructure. It is recommended that SA needs to adopt best practices to expand rural 5G access. This paper aims to contribute to ongoing discussions on policy measures to bridge the digital divide through enhanced mobile broadband coverage and connectivity.

articleTitle: Early Detection of Alzheimer's Disease through Speech-Text Analysis: A Review
publicationTitle: 2024 International Conference on IT Innovation and Knowledge Discovery (ITIKD)
abstract: Alzheimer's Disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder that poses a significant challenge for early diagnosis and effective treatment. While Magnetic Resonance Imaging (MRI) scans are commonly used for diagnosing AD, they often detect the disease at a later stage when brain damage has already occurred, limiting their effectiveness for early detection. In contrast, non-invasive diagnostic methods, particularly those based on speech analysis, have shown potential for identifying AD in its early stages. This review paper examines the role of machine learning techniques in analyzing speech patterns to detect early signs of AD.
